messages:
Maya (CSM): Weekly check-in for Cobalt cohort — quick pulse: tokens WoW +18%, QoQ +40%. Avg tokens/request jumped from ~350 -> ~500. Throughput (requests/s) up ~24% at peak. p95 latency now ~210ms (was 160ms last week). 5xx rate ~0.8% (still <1%). Spend projection +22% WoW if trend continues. Any immediate flags?

Devon (SRE): Noted. Is the throughput increase driven by higher RPS or longer sequences? Any batching changes?

Liam (Prod Eng): We rolled a prompt enrichment on Tue that adds more context per request — that explains the longer sequences. Also enabled dynamic batching on Wed but kept batch window conservative.

Ana (Account Lead): They're switching two more teams to prod this week (feature-flagged). We expected a ramp but unclear if they saw the cost impact. I flagged the account in CRM with a heads-up.

Maya (CSM): Ok — items to tackle: isolate whether queueing causes p95 jump vs token-length. Recommend an enablement call to review token profile + low-lift optimizations (prefix caching, input truncation, suggestion to shift some heavy jobs off-peak).

Devon (SRE): I'll look at GPU queue metrics and queue depth for the 11:00-12:30 PST peak. If queueing is the culprit we can adjust autoscale thresholds or suggest reserved capacity. Also can prepare a KV-prefix cache config that removes repeated system tokens.

Liam (Prod Eng): From quick glance at logs: average sequence length distribution shifted right — 20% more requests >512 tokens. That matches tokens/request numbers. Batching helps throughput but can increase latency for some single-request paths. We should consider smaller max batch or smart priority for low-latency routes.

Ana (Account Lead): Renewal watch: client has stretch targets on cost. If spend keeps rising >20% MoM without clear mitigations, finance might push discounts or ask for pricing re-eval. Mark as medium risk for Q1 renewal.

Maya (CSM): Proposed next steps: 1) 30m enablement call with Cobalt + us to walk token profile & quick wins; 2) Devon to share KV cache snippet and expected token savings; 3) Liam to analyze queueing by minute and propose autoscale tweak; 4) Ana to update AMs and flag renewal risk if numbers persist. Can we aim to complete 1-3 before Tuesday EOD? @Devon @Liam

Devon (SRE): Confirmed. I'll post config snippet here and a rough savings calc.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: scaling-policy update applied Wed 02:13 UTC (policy: dynamic-burst v2).

Devon (SRE): KV cache snippet: ```yaml
kv_cache:
  enabled: true
  prefix_keys: ["system_prompt_v3", "static_user_profile"]
  ttl_seconds: 3600
  expected_token_savings_pct: 28
```
Estimate: if client adopts prefix caching and reduces repeated context, tokens/request could drop ~20-30% depending on payload overlap.

Liam (Prod Eng): Queueing note: 11:00-12:00 PST shows 3x baseline queue depth on GPUs; p95 latency correlates with those spikes. Proposed autoscale tweak: decrease target utilization from 75% -> 65% during client peak window or offer reserved pool for predictable ramp. I'll put the detailed per-minute chart in the follow-up.

Maya (CSM): Great. I'll book the enablement slot for Tue 10:00am PT (tentative) and send calendar invite. Ana, I'll share the cost-impact slide for the client during the call.

Ana (Account Lead): Sounds good. I'll prep the customer-side usage narrative so they understand tradeoffs. If we can show a path to ~15% token reduction with caching+prompt trims, that should reduce renewal pressure.

Maya (CSM): Thanks — will update thread after call. Action owners: Devon -> KV snippet + savings; Liam -> queueing + autoscale proposal; Ana -> AM note + renewal flag.

Devon (SRE): Will do, dropping the config and expected savings by EOD today.

Liam (Prod Eng): I'll upload the minute-level charts and proposed autoscale change tomorrow morning.

Maya (CSM): Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
